question: Using Figure 2A-1 and Section 2A.11, describe the requirements for a retroreflective strip used on a sign support to enhance conspicuity.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Using a retroreflective strip on a sign support is a permitted (optional) method of enhancing sign conspicuity, chosen based on engineering judgment. When used, the strip must be at least 2 inches wide, run the full length of the support from the sign down to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, carry no legend, and match the sign's background color — except that the strip for YIELD and DO NOT ENTER signs must be red. A related mandatory application (white strip) exists for Crossbuck supports at passive grade crossings. Standards (mandatory): - "If a strip of retroreflective material is used on the sign support, it shall be at least 2 inches in width, it shall be placed for the full length of the support from the sign to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, and its color shall match the background color of the sign, except that the color of the strip for the YIELD and DO NOT ENTER signs shall be red. The retroreflective strip shall not display any legend or other information." - For passive grade crossings: "A vertical strip of retroreflective white material, not less than 2 inches in width, shall be used on each Crossbuck support at passive grade crossings for the full length of the back of the support from the Crossbuck sign or Number of Tracks plaque to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, except as provided in Paragraph 18 of this Section." A white strip wrapped around a round support of at least 2 inches outside diameter satisfies this requirement. Options (permitted): - Based upon engineering judgment, where improvement of the conspicuity of a standard regulatory, warning, or guide sign is desired, methods shown in Figure 2A-1 — including a vertical retroreflective strip on the sign support — may be used, as appropriate. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-1, panel E, illustrates a "Vertical retroreflective strip on sign support" beneath a fluorescent yellow-green pedestrian warning sign, with the strip color matching the sign background and a dimension callout of "2 ft MAX." between the bottom of the strip and the near edge of the roadway. - [Image 2] The full-page view of Figure 2A-1 (labeled Sect. 2A.11) shows the same panel E strip detail in the context of the seven conspicuity-enhancement examples (A–G). - [Image 3] Page 103 shows Section 2A.21 Support text noting that "Information regarding the use of retroreflective material on the sign support is contained in Section 2A.11." - [Image 4] Page 90 shows the Section 2A.11 Standard text (Paragraph 5) with the 2-inch width, full-length placement, color-matching, and no-legend requirements, plus item L listing the strip as a conspicuity method. - [Image 5] Page 1038 shows the Crossbuck Assembly figure with callouts for an "Optional 2-inch red or white retroreflective strip on front of support" and a required "2-inch white retroreflective strip on back of support," with the "2 ft MAX." dimension measured to the near edge of the roadway. Citations: - Section 2A.11 Standard §5 (p.49) - Section 2A.11 Option §1 (p.49) - Section 2A.21 Support §8 (p.62) - Section 8B.04 Standard §17 (p.1000) - Figure 2A-1 (p.48) - Page 89 - Page 90 - Page 103 - Page 1038
gold_answer: The strip must be at least 2 inches wide, extend from the sign down the full support to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, match the sign background color except that YIELD and DO NOT ENTER strips are red, and contain no legend or other information.
